text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Italian government may have begun moves to resolve a rift between Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas and Italian electricity generator ENEL, over the termination of a gas supply contract.
- Chairman of panel investigating November air crash of ADC Airlines Boeing-727 says that at the close of investigations it was not possible to pin-point the cause of the crash.

- The National Electric Power Authority plans to use fuel oil rather than gas to boost power generating capacity at its Egbin power station, supplying Lagos. The power station last week complained of a drop in gas pressure from the Nigerian Gas Company's pipeline from the Escravos field.
- Federal government plans to establish a crushing plant at Okaba Coal Mines in central Nigeria to process coal for export.

- Government may have started proceedings to extradite suspects of recent bomb blasts. Police are believed to be working towards extraditing members of the opposition National Democratic Coalition from self-exile in Europe and the United States.
- Fuel scarcity eases in commercial capital, Lagos, but spreads to surrounding states.
- Petroleum marketing companies have asked Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation to reconsider its decision that fuel should only be sold on a cash-and-carry basis.
- The World Bank may produce an official reaction to Nigeria's 1997 budget this weekend.

- A symposium of accountants has picked holes in the 1997 budget, saying it may fail to induce growth and development -- specifically because of the decision to slow privatisation and to keep the dual exchange rate mechanism.
